Chapter 10: The Invitation of Poetry—Living with Openness and Wonder.
Have you ever felt it? That sudden shift when a poem opens a door inside you, and suddenly, the world feels brighter and full of possibility?
It’s almost like the ordinary things around us become a little bit extraordinary. What you thought you knew feels fresh and a little bit mysterious.
That’s what poetry meant for Pablo Neruda. For him, it wasn’t just lines on a page—it was a way of living. Living with openness, with curiosity, with a sense of wonder.
Picture this: someone in the middle of a hectic day, pausing because a line of poetry caught their ear. Suddenly, all that noise drops away. There’s a little space to breathe. Maybe to feel something, or to remember what really matters. Poetry invites us to pay attention—to the sweetness of fruit, to the gentle rhythm of rain, to longing that lingers, to hope that simply won’t give up.
Most of us, let’s be honest, are on autopilot so much of the time. We miss the tiny miracles happening all around us. But poetry? It’s like a gentle tap on the shoulder, reminding us to wake up. To really look, to listen deeply.
It isn’t some fancy luxury—it’s a necessity. A way to stay alive to the world, a way to keep our hearts open, even when life feels overwhelming.
When you think about it, the invitation of poetry is both simple and profound. It asks us: can you be present? Will you notice what’s right in front of you? Will you care?
Poetry reminds us that beauty isn’t hiding. It’s everywhere, if we’re willing to see it. And while poems don’t always give us answers, they do offer something just as important—companionship. A sense that, whatever questions we’re carrying, whatever struggles or joys we’re living through, we’re not alone.
